question: When did an Indian chief minister hoist the national flag on Independence Day for the first time?
solution:
The correct answer is __**15th August 1974**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **15th August 1974**, an Indian Chief Minister hoisted the national flag on Independence Day for the first time.
 
• This event marked a significant moment in the history of India's Independence Day celebrations.
 
• Before this, the national flag on Independence Day was traditionally hoisted by the President of India at the national level and by Governors in their respective states.
 
• This change allowed Chief Ministers to play a more prominent role in the celebrations within their states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Independence Day in India is celebrated annually on **15th August**, commemorating the nation's independence from British rule in 1947.
 
• The day is observed with flag-hoisting ceremonies, parades, and cultural events across the country.
 
• The main event takes place at the Red Fort in Delhi where the Prime Minister addresses the nation.
 
• This tradition of flag hoisting by Chief Ministers has continued, reflecting the federal structure of India's democracy.
